newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares end bourse with modest gains.
newsitem.headline: German shares end bourse with modest gains.

text.p: German shares ended bourse dealings on Tuesday with modest gains as a stable overnight close on Wall Street and a firmer dollar took pressure off the domestic market.

The 30-share DAX index ended the bourse session up 5.74 points at 4,302.68 points, boosted in part by the dollar rising after the Bundesbank refrained from changing its interest rate policy in weekly money market activities.
The IBIS DAX, which reflects all-day computer dealings, later ended up 23.36 points at 4,325.86 points as the German market shrugged off early weakness on Wall Street.

Market dealings during the bourse session focused on the decision of the powerful Bundesbank to leave monetary policy on hold for the time being by keeping the securities repurchase rate, or repo rate, fixed at three percent.

Dealers had speculated the German central bank might have opted switch to a variable-rate repo, which allows banks to bid for funds and would have likely caused the repo rate to rise, to help curb the dramatic rise in the dollar against the mark.
But the decision kept the dollar on its upward path, which underpinned export-senstive shares since their products abroad will be cheaper.

Pharmaceuticals and chemical group Hoechst AG ended up 1.65 marks at 84.20 marks, while pharmaceuticals group Schering AG surged three marks to 203.50 marks and chemicals group BASF AG rose 10 pfennigs to 70.50 marks.
Airline Deutsche Lufthansa AG rose rose 60 pfennigs to 35.35 marks.
Banking shares remained in focus amid speculation of further industry mergers or takeovers after Vereinsbank and Hypo-Bank announced last month that they would merge.
Commerzbank AG rose 85 pfennigs to 62.35 marks but Deutsche Bank AG fell 50 pfennigs to 116.90 marks and Dresdner Bank AG slipped 1.50 marks to 79 marks.
